newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Arb cargoes threaten mogas.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Arb cargoes threaten mogas.

text.p: Both light distillates were steady on Wednesday despite softer crude amid good demand although gasoline might be due for some pressure on talk of arbitrage cargoes arriving in April, traders said.

A Japanese shosha was an active buyer in the Singapore market and bought a total of 280,000 barrels for March 27-April 1 lifting - two 50,000-barrel cargoes of unleaded 97-octane at $29.75 and $29.90 per barrel from a Swiss trader, and unleaded 92-octane at $28.70 for 80,000 barrels from anothe shosha and $28.95 for 50,000 barrels from the Swiss trader.
One trader said as much as up to one million barrels would be arriving in Singapore from the Mediterranean in April, with traders already offering cargoes in the market.
"With so much naphtha cargoes arriving, I wouldn't be surprised if some are partially mogas,' said a trader.
But another trader said it was unlikely as the arbitrage was closed.

A U.S. major was also bringing a Yanbu cargo from the Mideast to Singapore later this month, but it will mostly be used to cover the major's short as its Singapore 280,000-bpd refinery shuts down for turnaround mid-March for a month, a
source said.

The shutdown of Thailand's Star Petroleum Refining Co's 37,000 bpd residual fluid catalytic cracker (RFCC) for two weeks to March 24, will cause a gasoline shortfall. But current inventories with state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) were sufficient and it will not be seeking any imports for the time being.
But the market waited for clearer direction from the Saudi tender for April, which was due to be awarded as validity closed Wednesday.
Concerns had arisen earlier in the week on the total volume awarded. The tender sought up to 1.5 million barrels but high offers spurred talk of lower purchases.
Traders said offers for the 95-octane leaded gasoline were around $3-$5 per barrel over Singapore naphtha fob quotes, c-and-f Ras tanura on the Mideast Gulf.

Clearer direction on April fundamentals would also come to light in the close of Taiwan's import tender for 95-octane reformate for the second-half of the month which closes March 18 and is valid for two days.
Taiwan just last week purchased its April 1-15 requirements, 250,000-barrels each of leaded and unleaded reformate at close to $29.00 per barrel, c-and-f.

Taiwan has also awarded its tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of full range naphtha for April 1-20 delivery at just above $230.00 per tonne c-and-f Kaohsiung, lower than its last award at $239-$240 per tonne c-and-f March 11-20 delivery, a company official said.
The tender closed March 10 and was valid until March 12.
The official said the next CPC naphtha tender would be for May imports of naphthenic-and-aromatic (N+A) naphtha.

Sri Lanka issued a tender to sell 110,000-125,000 barrels of light naphtha for March 24-25 lifting fob Colombo, a company source said. The tender closes on March 18 and bids will be valid for two days.
Naphtha April swaps were steady at $22.95/$23.10 per barrel, May at $22.35/$22.45.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
